assumptions: Decoys are a fair null for the targets, and the search was the same for both.
limits: An FDR is a property of the whole set at a threshold, not a probability for one match.
The +1 and finite-sample corrections change the numbers, and the answer says which was used.
bio.jane/contract.question: What q-value does each peptide-spectrum match get by target-decoy competition, and how many pass a threshold?

description: False discovery rate and q-values for peptide-spectrum matches by target-decoy competition (validated against pyteomics): give each match's score and whether it hit a decoy; returns every match's q-value, the whole set's FDR, and how many targets pass a q-value threshold. Supports the +1 and finite-sample corrections of Levitsky et al. 2017.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

correction.description: 0 none; 1 the +1 correction; 2 finite-sample expectation; a value in (0, 1) is a confidence level.

formula.description: 1: decoys / targets. 2: (decoys + estimated false targets) / all matches.

higherIsBetter.description: true for scores like HyperScore; false for e-values and PEPs.

isDecoy.description: one flag per match: true when it is a decoy hit.

threshold.description: q-value cut-off for the accepted count.

name: target_decoy_qvalues

accepted.description: target matches at or under the q-value threshold

decoys.description: how many decoy matches were scored; the FDR estimate stands on this count

q.description: q-value per match, in input order

targets.description: how many target matches were scored

threshold.description: the q-value cut-off `accepted` was counted at
